why_serial_and_not_merely_ordered.why_a_merge_cannot_reconcile_them: Both packages change the ARITY and body of the same SECURITY DEFINER functions in the same schemas. A textual merge of two independent DROP+CREATE revisions of uellix_stella_ops.complete_operation_ticket produces a file that applies cleanly and installs a function neither author designed. stella_0018's self-verification asserts a function COUNT of exactly eight (E20); two concurrent revisions that each believe they preserved the count can jointly break it, and the failure surfaces only at apply time in a G2 window neither author controls.
why_serial_and_not_merely_ordered.direction_rationale: FIBDB-053 is first because it is the externally gated item (E5, E9, E10) and because its target is narrow and already frozen down to the parameter names. S3c is second because it is explicitly required to build from the LATEST FIBDB-053 form; the reverse order would force FIBDB-053 to re-derive a signature S3c had already moved.

s3c_preservation_obligations.rule: S3c builds FROM the latest FIBDB-053 form. It preserves each of the following exactly; changing any of them is a supersession of FIBDB-053, not an S3c change, and requires its own authority.
must_preserve: risk_level — the stella_interactions column, its CHECK vocabulary (NULL|low|medium|high) and its partial index (E21).
risk_flags — the text[] column and the fact that it is written on the same durable row, in the same transaction (E21).
The FINAL function signature FIBDB-053 publishes for the completion verb and for the settle function it delegates to — argument names, types and order.
Ticket-package semantics — one ticket is one unit whichever verb settles it; the charge identity is derived from a nonce no function returns; a caller cannot move the charge (E16).
Idempotency — the (organization_id, idempotency_key) contract and the ON CONFLICT ... DO NOTHING behaviour, unchanged (E14).
Quota transaction semantics — the charge, the ledger INSERT and the ticket status UPDATE remain in ONE transaction under the existing per-organization advisory lock (E14, E16).
s3c_preservation_obligations.reciprocal_prohibition: FIBDB-053 must NOT attempt to anticipate or implement S3c. It does not add an organization-scope recheck, does not change how organization_id is derived, and does not touch the selected-organization carrier. Those are S3c's obligations under the tenancy authority and remain there.

TWO_FUNCTION_DERIVATION.what_the_executable_state_shows: Those two clauses do not describe the same function. The advisory lock and the ledger INSERT with its ON CONFLICT live in uellix_stella.settle_reserved_quota, the TEN-argument function (E13, E14). The verb the runtime calls is uellix_stella_ops.complete_operation_ticket, the SEVEN-argument function, which owns neither the lock nor the INSERT and reaches them only by calling settle (E12, E16).
TWO_FUNCTION_DERIVATION.derived_contract: FIBDB-053 Stage A must revise a CHAIN of functions, not one function. The parameters are threaded, not merely added:

chain.change: DROP the ten-argument signature and CREATE a twelve-argument one adding p_risk_level varchar(50) and p_risk_flags text[], in the same transaction. The two new values are written into the SAME INSERT column list at E14 — never a second statement, never an UPDATE after the fact, because an UPDATE would edit an append-only trail and a second INSERT would be a second charge.
chain.invariants_preserved: The advisory lock stays first; the ON CONFLICT (organization_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL clause is unchanged; the function stays SECURITY DEFINER with SET search_path = ''; ownership stays uellix_cap_stella_quota; EXECUTE stays granted to uellix_cap_stella_ticket and to nobody else.

chain.change: Re-created so its body delegates to the NEW twelve-argument form with two additional NULLs. Its own signature does not change.
chain.why_it_cannot_be_skipped: E15 — the delegator's body names the ten-argument function explicitly. Dropping the ten-argument form without re-creating the delegator leaves a delegator pointing at a function that no longer exists, and the stated design reason for the delegator is that this schema holds ONE ledger INSERT reached by two arities. A missed delegator is a second body waiting to drift.

chain.change: DROP the seven-argument signature and CREATE a nine-argument one adding p_risk_level varchar(50) and p_risk_flags text[], passing both through to the twelve-argument settle at the call site measured at E16.
chain.invariants_preserved: Every refusal ordering is unchanged: identifier validation, project mismatch U0110 checked BEFORE the replay short-circuit, digest U0107, liveness U0108, replay semantics, and the derivation of the charge key from the unreturned nonce. Ownership stays uellix_cap_stella_ticket; EXECUTE stays granted to uellix_app.

TWO_FUNCTION_DERIVATION.no_overload_rule: Every one of the three is a DROP-then-CREATE inside one transaction, never a CREATE OR REPLACE with a longer argument list and never a DEFAULT. E5 gives the reason (CREATE OR REPLACE cannot alter the argument list; a DEFAULT creates an overload and raises the function count) and E20 gives the enforcement: stella_0018 asserts uellix_stella_ops holds EXACTLY EIGHT functions, and separately asserts that none of the four ticket verbs declares pronargdefaults > 0. Both assertions must still hold after stella_0017b.
TWO_FUNCTION_DERIVATION.function_count_after: uellix_stella_ops must still hold exactly EIGHT functions. The DROP+CREATE of complete_operation_ticket is count-neutral by construction; a package that leaves nine has created an overload and is refused by stella_0018's own verification if that unit is ever re-applied.

SOD.no_mandatory_third_person: The reviewer may also perform the narrative attestation and lock the report when permitted. The independence rule constrains WHO may approve, not HOW MANY people must touch the run (E2).

NO_SECOND_QUALIFIED_REVIEWER_PATH.rule: An organisation without a second authorised user MAY work with preliminary results but MAY NOT approve or lock. The condition is surfaced as the reason code NO_SECOND_QUALIFIED_REVIEWER — it is never a silent failure and never a generic permission error.

HIGH_FINDING_DISPOSITION.rule: Every risk_level='high' finding from an EXECUTED Stella review becomes a tracked open item requiring explicit human disposition, with justification, before run approval or report lock.
HIGH_FINDING_DISPOSITION.vocabulary_owner: FIBDB-049 (Stella findings/dispositions/abstentions vocabularies), owned by FIBIU-20 and consumed by FIBIU-21.
HIGH_FINDING_DISPOSITION.state_tables: FIBDB-019 stella_findings and FIBDB-020 stella_finding_dispositions, both NEW_TABLE, both append-only. Measured at AS_OF_HEAD: neither exists in db/schema.ts.
HIGH_FINDING_DISPOSITION.fail_closed: An open undisposed high finding BLOCKS approval and BLOCKS lock (E3).

ZERO_STELLA_ZERO_FINDING_GATE.rule: If Stella was NOT executed, NO finding gate is created.
ZERO_STELLA_ZERO_FINDING_GATE.source: E3, verbatim: 'If Stella was not executed (V-17), no such gate is created.'

ZERO_STELLA_ZERO_FINDING_GATE.why_this_needs_saying: The natural implementation of a blocking gate is 'block unless a disposition row exists', which converts every non-Stella run into a permanently blocked run. The gate is conditional on EXECUTION, not on the presence of a disposition.
ZERO_STELLA_ZERO_FINDING_GATE.test_obligation: A run with zero Stella interactions must be provably eligible on that dimension. This is a required negative control, not an optional one.

HUMAN_APPROVAL_BOUNDARY.rule: AI proposes and analyses; the system controls and calculates; humans decide and approve. Nothing in FIBIU-20 moves any part of that line.
specifics: No Stella output constitutes approval, certification, audit or external verification.

Stella does not approve a finding's resolution.

No automatic path may discharge a high finding — not a timeout, not a re-run, not a lower subsequent risk_level.
